gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-kr: Brush-drawn and unfussy, Origami looks like one marker stroke per letter, with no swelling anywhere. Noto Sans KR follows with a big x-height and stubby ascenders, leaving the curves generously open beneath that heavy heading.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lao: Single-stroke and sign-painted, Origami reads like following one continuous thread across the line. And Noto Sans Lao does the quieter work, with a tall x-height and mouths that stay open on c, e and a.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lao-loop: Origami's strokes are straight-edged and constant, like bent wire. Noto Sans Lao Looped settles beneath it with words that form solid blocks rather than jagged skylines, and bowls left open on one side.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lepcha: Origami has zero stroke contrast, just a heavy lowercase mass drawn like poured lead. Noto Sans Lepcha is the foil here, a plain sans whose wide-open curves and cast-iron stature in the lowercase make the two feel sturdy together.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-limbu: Origami looks marker-drawn, with a plainness in every character and a lowercase like poured lead type. Noto Sans Limbu brings the strongest quality: tall small letters with gaping curves, friendly beside it.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lisu: Monoline and brushy, Origami keeps every stroke the same. It handles bold, poured-lead headings best, while Noto Sans Lisu, a plain sans with wide-open s curves and tight gaps at the ascender tops, handles the running text.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-lydian: Noto Sans Lydian reads softly, with capitals barely taller than the lowercase and an opening wide as a sprung paper clip. Over a long passage it stays easygoing, while Origami's bent-pipe strokes of constant width give the heading its muscle.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mahajani: Contemporary and blunt, Origami draws its crossbars as thick as its stems. Noto Sans Mahajani lifts the lowercase tall against its capitals and flares the e like a funnel, so the two feel like a shout and a chat.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-malayala: Origami is a sign-painter's brush at constant width, with no swelling in any curve of its poured-lead lowercase. It grabs attention best; Noto Sans Malayalam, a plain sans with a dominant middle zone, carries the text.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-noto-sans-mandaic: Origami never presses harder anywhere, so the eye has no swell to slow down on. Noto Sans Mandaic brings the pair's strongest quality, a sans-serif with lowercase rising close to its capitals and loose, unclamped curves.
